subject.title: [Feature]: Add gateway-side circuit breaker for unhealthy sessions after consecutive failures

question: Should OpenClaw add a core session-health circuit breaker for arbitrary repeated no-progress session failures, and should that include persisted health receipts plus configurable recovery policy rather than only extending the existing idle-timeout/provider-cooldown guards?
rationale: The remaining work changes core retry admission, persisted session state, operator-visible recovery, and possibly config defaults; source inspection shows a real gap, but automation should not choose those product and compatibility contracts.

options.title: Sponsor a core session-health design
options.body: Define a narrow receipt/state-machine contract first, then implement the breaker against current retry/fallback/session-store paths with focused upgrade and UI proof.

options.title: Limit scope to existing guards
options.body: Close or narrow this issue after deciding that idle-timeout, provider cooldown, compaction, and tool-loop guards are the intended product boundary for now.

options.title: Split into narrower follow-ups
options.body: Keep this issue as context but move specific failure classes such as context overflow, rate-limit loops, and auto-rotation into separate implementation issues.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core session-health design
recommendation.body: Define a narrow receipt/state-machine contract first, then implement the breaker against current retry/fallback/session-store paths with focused upgrade and UI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current retry-guard and session-suspension code most recently routes through Vincent Koc's blamed changes, so he is the best available owner to decide whether this belongs in core runtime state.
